name: Task Flick
summary: A phone recent-apps screen: pull the open app into a card, fan through the rest and flick them away
about: The app switcher of a phone, built so every move feels physical. Swipe up from the home bar and the open app shrinks under your finger; hold for a beat and the other recent apps slide in from the left as an angled, overlapping fan, while a quick flick sends the app back into its home-screen icon instead. In the switcher you drag through the cards with momentum, flick one up to close it while the others close the gap, tap one to zoom it open, or clear them all in a cascade.
how: Drag up from the bar at the bottom and pause: the app becomes a card and the other recent apps fan in. Let go to stay in the switcher.
Flick up quickly instead to go home: the app shrinks into its icon and the home screen pops in.
In the switcher, drag sideways to browse, flick a card up to close it, tap a card to open it, or press Clear all.
Tap any icon on the home screen to open that app again; it moves to the front of your recent apps.
Keyboard: the Home and Recent apps buttons sit at the bottom; in the switcher the arrow keys move, Enter opens and Delete closes the focused card.
